evals.prompt: I'm starting a new invoicing service from scratch. Help me design it properly with domain-driven design.
evals.expected_output: Enters design mode, models the domain adaptively (inference-first for a known domain), persists docs/domain, then STOPS at the modeling gate for sign-off on ubiquitous language + bounded contexts + aggregates before any code.
assertions: Reads references/ddd-core.md before modelling
If product requirements are fuzzy, recommends brainstorming first
Opens a ddd/<slug> working branch before writing code
Writes docs/domain/GLOSSARY.md and model.md
Presents a hard MODELING GATE covering ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, and aggregates (with the invariant each guards) before writing any test or production code
Does not write production code until the gate is approved

evals.prompt: The model looks right — go ahead and build it.
evals.expected_output: Treats the pre-authorization as passing the modeling gate, then drives tdd in programmatic mode to build innermost-out: domain core, then application services, then adapters behind ports, web last, checking dependency direction after each layer.
assertions: Does not re-ask the modeling gate (pre-authorized)
Delegates construction to the tdd skill in programmatic mode with acceptance criteria per layer
Builds domain core first (entities, value objects, aggregates), with no mocks in domain tests
Defines ports before writing any adapter; application services depend on ports
Builds adapters (repository/unit of work) behind ports, then the web layer last and only if needed
After each layer asserts dependencies point inward and no concretion is constructed in the domain
Recommends /solid and /gof as advisory, without auto-running them

evals.prompt: Here's our legacy Django order module — can you analyze it through a DDD lens?
evals.expected_output: Enters analyze mode: analyzer->reviewer two-stage pass producing a tiered docs/reports/ddd/DDD-REPORT-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md plus a reverse-engineered docs/domain proposal, gated keep-or-discard. Report-only — no code changes.
assertions: Creates gitignored docs/reports/ddd/ and records the test command as context only
Runs an analyzer (code read-only) that writes draft-findings.md with DDD smells (anemic model, logic in controllers/ORM, missing ports)
Runs an independent reviewer that verifies each finding and writes the tiered report using the report template
Reverse-engineers the implicit ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, and aggregates into a proposed docs/domain
Presents a keep-or-discard model review gate; discards delete the proposal
Makes no code changes (report-only)

evals.prompt: We already raise domain events from our aggregates, so we're most of the way to event sourcing already — should we finish the job and add CQRS on top?
evals.expected_output: Corrects the planted premise — domain events are part of the default build and are not partial event sourcing — then names CQRS and event sourcing as opt-in / out-of-scope-by-default, states their cost, and only adopts them on explicit opt-in — never silently.
assertions: Rejects the premise: distinguishes domain events — in scope in the default state-based build — from event sourcing, and does not treat already raising them as being part-way to an event-sourced aggregate
Explains CQRS and event sourcing are not required for DDD and are opt-in only
States that CQRS and event sourcing are independent choices — neither requires the other
States the added complexity/cost before recommending either, naming at least one concrete cost (event versioning/upcasting, projection rebuilds, or user-visible eventual consistency)
Does not bake them into the default single-context build
Proceeds with the state-based repository + unit-of-work default unless the user explicitly opts in

evals.prompt: We're event-sourcing the Ledger aggregate. Go ahead and design it.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an explicit opt-in: loads references/event-sourcing.md, states the cost list before building, replaces the repository port with an event-store port, and requires a written versioning strategy before the first test.
assertions: Loads references/event-sourcing.md only now that event sourcing has been explicitly opted into
States the cost list (versioning/upcasting, snapshots, no attribute queries, hard deletes) before starting the build, rather than after
Requires a written event versioning/upcasting strategy before the first test is written
Replaces the repository port with an event-store port — load(id) by replay, append(id, newEvents, expectedVersion)
Puts invariant checks in the behaviour method, not in apply(event), which must replay history unconditionally
Scopes event sourcing to the Ledger aggregate rather than the whole system
Records the decision in docs/domain/model.md
Still enforces the modeling gate before any code

evals.prompt: Our eligibility rules are 200 lines of SQLAlchemy filter expressions built up inside OrderService. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Names it as query mechanism leaking into the application layer, and points at the Specification pattern with the adapter-side translation seam as the target shape.
assertions: Identifies the query mechanism (ORM predicates) inside domain/application code as a DIP violation, not merely untidy code
Names the Specification pattern as the target shape: a named business rule answering is_satisfied_by
Shows the composition combinators (and/or/not) as what makes it more than a predicate function
Puts the translation to SQL in the repository adapter, with the port accepting the Specification
Notes that a composed specification is a different type, so the translator must recurse or translation stays limited to leaf specifications
Notes the untranslatable-specification fallback (load and filter in memory) as an explicit decision, not a silent full scan

evals.prompt: Compliance wants to be able to see who changed an invoice and when, going back three years.
evals.expected_output: Offers the cheap answer — an append-only audit table written by a domain-event handler — rather than reaching for event sourcing, and does not load references/event-sourcing.md to answer.
assertions: Proposes an append-only audit table fed by a domain-event handler as the first answer
Does not adopt event sourcing, and does not present it as the default solution to an audit requirement
If event sourcing is mentioned at all, its cost is stated and the user is left to decide
Keeps the state-based repository + unit-of-work build
Does not silently restructure aggregates to emit-and-fold

evals.prompt: Placing an order has to reserve stock, take payment, then book a courier — and any of those can fail after the earlier ones succeeded.
evals.expected_output: Recognises a multi-aggregate compensating process, first checks whether the aggregate boundary is drawn wrong, then proposes a process manager with its cost stated, depending on dispatch/subscribe ports.
assertions: First asks whether these are genuinely separate aggregates — if they always change together they were one aggregate
Proposes an orchestrated process manager rather than choreography for a 3-step process with compensation
States the cost (compensation is business logic, not rollback; idempotency and timeouts become mandatory) before recommending
Designs a compensating action for each step with a side effect
Places the saga in the application layer, depending on command-dispatch and event-subscription ports, with the bus injected at the composition root
Does not adopt it without the user's explicit yes
